bullets.title: NVDA: $500B AI financing plan, Nemotron releases, HBM downspec optionality, IBM deal
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced a $500B+ third-party AI financing plan with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, GS, and KKR to drive chip demand without NVDA balance sheet usage. Separately, NVDA released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (30B MoE, open-source) and is developing Nemotron 4 (1T+ parameters). One analyst estimates a broad HBM downspec across Rubin could enable 30–50% more GPU shipments from the same HBM supply. IBM signed a $240M deal with Together AI to deploy NVIDIA HGX B300 clusters on IBM Cloud (Q1 2027). Systematic buyers (Citadel) are reportedly ready to add exposure as leverage unwinds complete.

bullets.title: LITE: Strong Q4 beat/raise; stock down on expectations bar — JPM and UBS both positive
bullets.body: Lumentum Q4 revenue beat at $1.10B vs. consensus $988M; guided Q1 to $1.225–1.275B midpoint (24% sequential growth). EPS beat by 28c vs. JPM buyside bars and gross margin beat consensus by 610bps at 50.4%. UBS highlighted broad-based OCS and cloud module traction with 1.6T adoption and CPO laser demand. Stock down ~0.4% despite the solid print, likely due to high expectations — JPM notes market was pricing $1.3B+ guide.

bullets.title: SMCI: Q4 beat and massive FY27 raise on $60B new orders; margins expand sharply
bullets.body: Super Micro Q4 revenue $11.1B beat guidance; EPS $1.70 vs. consensus $0.92. FY27 guidance raised to $65–72B vs. prior consensus $52.99B, driven by $60B in new orders and record backlog. Gross margin expanded to 17.6% from 9.9% YoY, and EBITDA margin improved to 15% from 5.8% on DCBBS architecture and enterprise mix.

bullets.title: CRWV: Q2 inline revenue with $104B backlog and accelerating enterprise demand
bullets.body: CoreWeave Q2 revenue $2.58B was in line; EPS and EBITDA ($1.51B, 59% margin) beat guidance. Backlog reached ~$104B plus >$425B in Q3 commitments. UBS cites accelerating customer demand and broadening enterprise adoption. Stock was +13.6% after-hours on the print.

bullets.title: AMD: 80%+ server CPU growth guided for H2 2026; Helios ramp driving billions in revenue
bullets.body: At KeyBanc forum, AMD guided server CPU revenue growth >80% in H2 2026 and >70% in 2027, led by Venice CPUs with Helios rack shipments starting September. Multi-gigawatt commitments from OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic through early 2028. Company targets 50%+ server CPU market share by 2030 ($220B TAM). Jefferies rates AMD Buy with $650 PT.

bullets.title: INTC: $20B share sale oversubscribed; unusual $5M+ call flow; foundry AI narrative intact
bullets.body: Intel priced a $20B equity offering that was multiple times oversubscribed — roughly 1 in 3 investors received no shares. CEO frames the offering as capital to fund AI foundry expansion, priced into a rally rather than in distress. Separately, $5M+ in unusual call options activity detected. Jefferies holds Intel at HOLD with $120 PT.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini reaches 1B+ monthly users, Google's 14th product to hit that milestone
bullets.body: Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced Gemini surpassed 1 billion monthly active users, calling it Google's fastest-growing product ever and its 14th to reach the 1B-user milestone. Separately, S&P 1500 Communications Services Index fell 2.1% with GOOGL as a major detractor.

bullets.title: APP: BofA downgrades to Neutral, cuts PT to $400 from $430; stock down ~6%
bullets.body: Bank of America downgraded AppLovin to Neutral from Buy and cut the price target to $400 from $430, citing risks to the 40% revenue growth trajectory. Stock declined 6.0% on the day. The Communications Services advertising segment was the weakest sector group, down 3.7%.

bullets.title: Jefferies semis analyst roadshow: BUY AVGO, NVDA, AMD, COHR, CRDO, LITE, MRVL, MTSI, SNDK
bullets.body: Jefferies' Blayne Curtis is conducting a NYC analyst roadshow September 2–3 covering post-earnings themes and AI infrastructure outlook. Buy ratings: AMD ($650 PT), NVDA ($300 PT), AVGO ($550 PT), COHR ($375 PT), CRDO ($270 PT), ALAB ($450 PT), MRVL ($325 PT), LITE ($1,200 PT), MTSI ($450 PT), SNDK ($1,750 PT). Hold ratings: INTC ($120 PT), TXN ($260 PT).

bullets.title: AAPL: Pay/Wallet exec departure in October; India manufacturing ramp; all-glass iPhone 2027
bullets.body: Apple's executive overseeing Pay and Wallet services is departing in October. The company is aggressively boosting iPhone production in India to hedge against China risk. Reports also indicate Apple planning an all-glass iPhone for 2027. Stock was down on the day as part of broader Mag 7 weakness.

bullets.title: TSMC: Record July revenue as AI fills every wafer slot; CoWoS near capacity
bullets.body: TSMC reported record July revenue with AI demand filling every wafer slot. Discussions at OCP APAC highlighted CoWoS packaging constraints — TSMC is close to but not fully meeting demand. No formal guidance change but the data point supports AI infrastructure capex thesis.

bullets.title: MU, SNDK: Memory supply tighter longer; data-center demand supports pricing
bullets.body: At the Future of Memory and Storage Conference 2026, the takeaway was that memory ASP flattening does not signal oversupply — higher contract spot price (CSP) LTA mix will support pricing. Data-center demand is the key driver keeping memory tight. Systematic buyers (Citadel) reportedly ready to add MU, SNDK exposure as leverage unwind completes.

bullets.title: ORCL: CDS spreads back above 200bps; Oracle-Quantinuum quantum partnership announced
bullets.body: Oracle CDS spreads widened back above 200 basis points, flagged as a notable credit stress signal. Separately, Oracle announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Quantinuum, giving OCI customers access to Helios quantum computing alongside HPC/GPU infrastructure.

bullets.title: DLR: +8.7% on earnings day; data centers most crowded REIT sector per Citi
bullets.body: Digital Realty was the top REIT performer on earnings day (+8.7%), per Citi's 2Q26 REIT wrap. Citi notes Data Center REITs and Storage REITs as the best-performing sectors since mid-July earnings. Data Centers are also the most crowded REIT sector in Citi's August factor analysis.

bullets.title: FSLR: Upgraded to Outperform at Baird, PT raised to $318 from $205
bullets.body: Baird upgraded First Solar to Outperform and raised its price target to $318 from $205. Utilities and energy were top sector gainers as the broader S&P 500 declined 0.3%, with NNE +4.4%, OKLO +5.6%, and TLN +4.3% also outperforming.

bullets.title: AMZN: Far-dated put selling signals bullish positioning; Trump-Snow trade flags governance risk
bullets.body: Millions in far-dated AMZN 2027 put-selling reflects bullish long-term conviction. Separately, Trump's May 21 purchase of SNOW preceded an Amazon AI deal by less than a week — stock up 94% since — raising insider trading questions. Morgan Stanley's internet team rates AMZN attractive, stock +1% on the day.

bullets.title: TSLA: Most bullish options flow of the day; Morgan Stanley: Robotaxi proof needed
bullets.body: TSLA showed the most bullish options flow among tracked names on Tuesday. Morgan Stanley states Tesla must demonstrate clear Robotaxi scaling evidence to maintain investor confidence, while noting that stronger FSD adoption supports the physical AI narrative.

bullets.title: MPWR: Analyst initiates Buy with $1,706 PT on AI power demand and design wins
bullets.body: A buy initiation on Monolithic Power with a $1,706 price target cites key positioning in AI GPU and ASIC power (VPD module uplift), firm DrMOS pricing, and design wins in storage, enterprise data, and auto. EPS forecast $28 for 2026E.

bullets.title: SHOP: Strong Q2 GMV +32% YoY; UBS highlights payments momentum and upgraded outlook
bullets.body: Shopify Q2 GMV grew 32% YoY (30% FXN) with revenue and gross profit each up ~32%/30% FXN. Q3 revenue guided to low-30s% YoY growth. UBS flags SHOP as showing notable strength within payments/fintech and reiterates constructive view on V and MA as most preferred large-cap payments.

bullets.title: DKNG: CFTC invokes emergency authority to shield Kalshi prediction markets from NY AG
bullets.body: The CFTC used emergency authority to protect Kalshi prediction markets after NY AG filed a complaint seeking $36B in damages. CFTC Chairman Selig stated New York has no jurisdiction over CFTC-regulated derivatives exchanges. CFTC has filed suit against 9 states attempting to regulate its exchanges — a potential competitive read-through for DKNG's online gaming regulatory environment.
